scope: SQLite official CLI documentation (cli.html) and the 3.53.0 release notes; exact command set is version-scoped

claims.claim: The sqlite3 command-line program is a separate application from the SQLite library; dot-commands are interpreted by the CLI and will not work as arguments to sqlite3_prepare() or sqlite3_exec()
.tables is approximately SELECT name FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type IN ('table','view') AND name NOT LIKE 'sqlite_%' ORDER BY 1, but also covers all attached databases and arranges output in columns
.schema and .indexes are convenience shortcuts; .schema shows the whole schema or one table, .indexes lists indexes (optionally for a table)
The .mode command controls result formatting; .mode --list lists modes, .mode shows the current mode, and .mode --once box applies a mode to the next statement only
SQLite 3.53.0 added the Query Result Formatter (QRF) library used for CLI result formatting; interactive sessions default to box output and numeric values are right-justified
claims.notes: Replaces the earlier chapter's invented QRFormatter struct and 3.54.0 streaming claims

claims.claim: .dump writes the whole database as a UTF-8 SQL text file that can be piped back into sqlite3 to rebuild it; .recover is the analogue for a corrupted database
shell.c is generated from src/shell.c.in (regenerate with 'make shell.c') and compiled together with the library sources, e.g. gcc -o sqlite3 shell.c sqlite3.c -ldl -lpthread -lz -lm
claims.notes: Replaces the earlier chapter's invented line-count table and aDotCommands callback array

claims.claim: When sqlite3 is started with a database name and one SQL argument, it runs that SQL, prints results in list mode and exits; this makes it easy to use from shell scripts
claims.locator: 21. Using sqlite3 in a shell script
